setFeedback.priority: Actual performance overrides star rating when the two conflict.

loadFirst.completedTarget_stars1: increase load about 5-7.5%; keep rep target
loadFirst.completedTarget_stars2: increase load by smallest practical increment to about 2.5-5%; keep rep target
loadFirst.completedTarget_stars4: hold load; keep reps if workout target is Hard/Insane, otherwise reduce next target by 1 rep
loadFirst.completedTarget_stars5: reduce load about 5%; keep or reduce target by 1 rep
loadFirst.missedBy1: usually hold load and reduce next target by 1 rep; if star=5, reduce load 2.5-5%
loadFirst.missedBy3Plus: reduce load about 7.5-10%; flag performance collapse if repeated

repsFirst.completedTarget_stars1: same load, add 2 reps within legal intent zone
repsFirst.completedTarget_stars2: same load, add 1-2 reps within legal intent zone
repsFirst.completedTarget_stars4: hold load; reduce next target by 1 rep if workout target is below Hard
repsFirst.completedTarget_stars5: reduce load one increment or reduce target 1-2 reps
repsFirst.missedTarget: actual performance governs; reduce target and/or load using miss size before subjective stars

freshnessRules.0to14Days: high confidence; recent exercise-specific history can set the next week's first working load
freshnessRules.15to28Days: lower confidence; start about 5% below the history-derived normalized load and recalibrate
freshnessRules.29PlusDays: stale; do not assume old strength remains. Re-seed conservatively using current bodyweight/experience plus stale history as a ceiling, then rebuild confidence.
freshnessRules.largeBodyweightChange: Lower confidence for bodyweight skills and relative-strength movements when bodyweight changes materially.
freshnessRules.newExerciseVariation: Use predetermined related-exercise transfer rule or statistical seed; exact prior exercise history does not transfer 1:1.

week2PlusStartLoadRule.summary: Normalize the previous session's trustworthy load for prior workout difficulty, adjust for performance trend, then apply the new workout difficulty multiplier.
week2PlusStartLoadRule.referenceSet: Prefer a recent successful working set at/above its prescribed reps with a 2-4 star rating; ignore obvious outliers.

trendAdjustment.allSetsCompleted_avgStars1to2: +5% compound anchor; +one practical increment on isolation/reps-first work
trendAdjustment.allSetsCompleted_avgStarsAbout3: +2.5% on load-first anchor lifts; reps-first exercises generally begin at the prior load
trendAdjustment.any5StarOrMeaningfulMiss: start 2.5-5% lower depending on miss size

week2PlusStartLoadRule.difficultyNormalization: normalizedLoad = priorStartLoad / priorDifficultyMultiplier; newStartLoad = normalizedLoad * trendAdjustment * currentDifficultyMultiplier

hypertrophyProgressionContract.purpose: Keep every progressive-overload decision inside the movement-specific hypertrophy rep zone while adapting exact reps and load set-to-set and week-to-week.
hypertrophyProgressionContract.workingSetTarget: Most hypertrophy working sets should finish at 3-4 stars. Five-star/grinder sets are not intentionally prescribed.
setToSetAlgorithm: Read actual reps, 1-5 star difficulty, and form validity from the completed set.
If form failed, treat the set as unsuccessful regardless of the star rating.
If actual reps fall below the movement's repFloor, reduce load by the smallest practical amount; use a larger reduction for a large miss. Never compensate by prescribing sub-floor reps.
If reps are inside the legal range and difficulty is about 3 stars, normally hold the load and progress only when the movement's priority supports it.

For reps_first movements, add 1-2 reps while remaining <= repCeiling. Once repCeiling is achieved cleanly at <=3 stars, add the smallest practical load increment and reset the target into the lower half of the range.
For load_first movements, an easy successful set may receive the smallest practical load increase only if the predicted next-set target remains >= repFloor. If not, hold load and add reps instead.
At 4 stars, normally hold load; adjust target reps inside the legal range if needed.
At 5 stars or after a meaningful miss, reduce next-set load and/or reps while staying inside the legal range.
Actual performance always overrides subjective star feedback when they conflict.
betweenWorkoutAlgorithm: Use the freshest trustworthy working-set history, not warm-up sets, as the primary reference.
Normalize the prior starting load for prior workout difficulty, apply the performance trend, then apply the current workout difficulty multiplier.
The resulting prescription must still pass the movement's repFloor/repCeiling guardrail.
Warm-up Sets 1-2 may refine confidence/readiness but never become the primary strength estimate.
Set 3 on integrated-anchor lifts is the calibration working set; Sets 4-5 adapt from it.
Week 4 is a recovery pivot: use the programmed reduced set counts, Easy/Normal only, and do not chase load PRs.
Weeks 5-7 resume accumulation from the freshest successful normalized history.
Week 8 consolidates/compares clean performance; do not force failure to prove progression.
hypertrophyProgressionContract.loadIncrementRule: Use the smallest practical increment available on that specific piece of equipment. Never invent unavailable microloading.
hypertrophyProgressionContract.warmupExclusion: Integrated warm-up sets count toward session tonnage but not hypertrophy hard-set totals and do not directly drive progressive overload.
hypertrophyProgressionContract.timedAndSkillExclusion: Skills, cardio, cooldowns, vacuums, and recovery movements use their own quality/duration rules and are excluded from hypertrophy load progression unless explicitly marked core_hypertrophy.

Alternate sides without rushing.

setup: Stand tall with light support available if needed.
howTo: Alternate easy steps and slow ankle circles when each foot is unloaded.
Keep circles controlled rather than forcing end range.

setup: Stand about shoulder width with toes comfortable.
howTo: Sit into a shallow comfortable squat, stand, and reach arms overhead.
Use smooth breathing and stop well before fatigue.

setup: Stand tall and begin a gentle march.
howTo: Rotate the ribcage gently toward the stepping side while hips remain mostly forward.
Keep range comfortable.

setup: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed.
howTo: Slowly rotate the head right and left through a pain-free range.
Keep chin level and avoid forcing end range.

setup: Stand tall with ribs stacked and one arm free.
howTo: Move one arm through the largest slow pain-free circle you can control.
Keep torso still; reverse direction and switch arms.

setup: Stand or kneel tall with arms relaxed.
howTo: Move shoulder blades up, back, down, and forward in a slow circle.
Reverse direction without bending the spine excessively.

setup: Stand tall with elbows near sides.
howTo: Slowly flex and extend elbows, then rotate palms up and down through comfortable range.
Keep shoulders relaxed.

setup: Hold forearm still with hand relaxed.
howTo: Draw slow wrist circles through comfortable range.
Reverse direction and repeat on the other wrist.

setup: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
howTo: Exhale and gently round the spine; inhale and extend through the spine without collapsing the low back.
Move one segment at a time when possible.

setup: Lie on one side with hips/knees bent and arms extended together.
howTo: Open the top arm across the body while knees stay stacked.
Follow the hand with your eyes, then return slowly.

setup: Stand beside a wall/chair for light support and brace the trunk.
howTo: Lift one knee, open it outward, rotate the hip, then return through a slow controlled circle.
Use the largest range that does not move the pelvis.

setup: Sit with knees bent and feet wider than hips.
howTo: Rotate both knees side to side into 90/90 positions without forcing depth.
Keep hands behind you if needed for support.

setup: Start on hands and knees and extend one leg to the side with foot planted.
howTo: Rock hips backward until the inner thigh stretches, then return forward.
Keep spine controlled.

setup: Stand with support available.
howTo: Slowly bend one knee to bring heel toward glute, then extend the leg without snapping the joint.
Alternate sides.

setup: Face a wall with one foot flat several inches away.
howTo: Drive knee toward wall over the toes while heel stays down, then return.
Adjust distance so motion stays controlled.

setup: Sit or stand with one foot unloaded.
howTo: Draw the largest slow ankle circle you can control without moving the whole leg.
Reverse direction.

setup: Take a comfortable squat stance and use a support if needed.
howTo: Sink only as deep as comfortable, shift gently side to side, and use elbows to create space at the hips.
Keep heels supported.

setup: Stand facing a wall with one foot slightly behind.
howTo: Keep heel down and pulse the knee/hips forward gently to move through ankle and calf range.
Stay smooth and pain-free.

setup: Stand tall with feet about hip width and support available.
howTo: Rise onto the balls of the feet over about 2 seconds, pause, and lower over about 3 seconds.
Keep pressure through the big-toe side of the forefoot.

setup: Lean upper back lightly against a wall with feet slightly forward and heels planted.
howTo: Lift toes toward shins while heels stay down, pause, then lower slowly.

setup: Take a short split stance with front foot flat and support nearby.
howTo: Drive front knee forward over toes while heel stays down, then return.
Use a small controlled range and no bouncing.

setup: Kneel on a padded surface with torso tall; use hands/support if needed.
howTo: Keeping hips extended, lean the whole body backward a small controlled distance, then return using the quads.
Use only a pain-free range.

setup: Lie on back with knees bent and feet flat.
howTo: Drive through feet, squeeze glutes, and lift hips until trunk and thighs form a line.
Hold without over-arching the low back.

setup: Start in a glute bridge with heels relatively close to hips.
howTo: Take small heel steps away while keeping hips controlled, then walk back in.
Stop before hamstrings cramp or pelvis drops.

setup: Stand on one leg with fingertips on a wall/chair and hinge slightly at the hip.
howTo: Rotate pelvis gently open and closed over the stance hip while keeping the knee stable.
Use support to prioritize hip control over balance.

setup: Take a plank or knees-down plank with elbows locked.
howTo: Let shoulder blades come slightly together, then push the floor away to protract them.
Do not turn it into an elbow push-up.

setup: Stand with back near a wall and forearms against it if comfortable.
howTo: Slide arms upward while keeping ribs controlled and shoulders away from ears.
Return slowly without forcing contact.

setup: Lie face down with forehead supported and arms free.
howTo: Lift arms slightly into Y, T, and W shapes using the upper back, not momentum.
Keep neck long and use a small controlled range.

setup: Start on hands and knees with fingers spread and palms flat.
howTo: Shift body weight gently forward/back and side-to-side while keeping pressure controlled.
Reduce lean if wrists feel irritated.

setup: From kneeling, place backs of hands lightly on the floor with very little bodyweight.
howTo: Gently straighten elbows only as comfortable, then unload.
Keep pressure minimal; this is mobility/capacity work, not a stretch contest.

setup: Stand barefoot if practical with tripod contact at heel, big-toe base, and little-toe base.
howTo: Gently draw the ball of the big toe toward the heel without curling the toes.
Hold the arch and breathe normally.

setup: Lie on side with bottom leg bent and top leg straight.
howTo: Lift top leg slightly behind the body without rolling the pelvis backward, pause, and lower slowly.

setup: Lie on back with hips/knees around 90 degrees and arms up.
howTo: Brace gently, lower opposite arm and leg without losing rib/pelvis position, then return and alternate.

setup: Stand tall with relaxed shoulders and enough space to march.
howTo: March smoothly at an easy recovery rhythm with natural arm swing.
Use this only for the 30-second active-recovery slot.

setup: Stand tall with feet under hips.
howTo: March briskly with purposeful arm swing while keeping impact low.
Keep breathing controlled at the programmed recovery effort.

setup: Stand with room to move side to side.
howTo: Step laterally, bring the other foot in to tap, then reverse direction.
Sweep arms naturally without turning it into jumping.

setup: Stand centered with clear floor space ahead.
howTo: Step forward and out with each foot to form the top of a V, then step back in to the start.
Keep rhythm smooth and low impact.

setup: Stand tall with knees soft.
howTo: Tap one heel forward while reaching arms comfortably, return, then alternate.
Keep weight shifts light and rhythmic.

setup: Stand tall with room behind you.
howTo: Step one foot back to a toe tap while pulling elbows back, return, then alternate.
Keep front knee soft and torso tall.

setup: Stand with several feet of side-to-side space.
howTo: Take two quick low-impact steps to one side, touch, then travel back.
Stay light without hopping.

setup: Stand tall with feet under hips.
howTo: Step and curl the opposite heel toward the glute while pulling elbows back, then alternate.
Keep knees pointing downward rather than flaring.

setup: Stand with clear lateral space.
howTo: Step to the side, cross the trailing foot behind, step side again, then tap and reverse.
Use a simple step-touch instead if coordination is poor.

setup: Stand centered with space at both front diagonals.
howTo: Step out diagonally, return to center, then alternate diagonals.
Keep steps controlled and low impact.

setup: Imagine a small square around your starting position.
howTo: Step through the four corners in a controlled pattern, then reverse direction halfway through.
Keep the square small enough to stay relaxed.

setup: Stand with feet about hip width.
howTo: Step laterally behind or beside the stance leg like a skater without jumping, then alternate.
Keep hips level and range comfortable.

setup: Stand tall with one foot ready to move.
howTo: Alternate tapping a foot forward and back while shifting rhythmically, switching lead naturally.
Keep taps light and continuous.

setup: Stand with feet slightly wider than hips and knees relaxed.
howTo: Shift weight side to side with small alternating steps like an easy boxer shuffle, without bouncing off the floor.
Keep it low impact.

setup: Stand tall and brace gently.
howTo: March while lifting each knee only to a comfortable height and driving the opposite arm.
Keep cadence brisk but conversational.

setup: Stand with room to move laterally.
howTo: Step to one side and lightly cross the trailing foot in front, then reverse.
Keep crossing shallow if hips/knees prefer it.

setup: Stand tall with feet about hip width, knees unlocked, and ribs stacked over pelvis.
howTo: Relax shoulders and jaw.
Inhale through the nose into belly/ribs and exhale slowly while staying tall.

setup: Stand tall and reach both arms overhead; clasp hands or hold the opposite wrist.
howTo: Reach upward first, then bend gently to one side without rotating the chest.
Return to center before switching sides.

setup: Stand feet hip width with knees softly bent.
howTo: Fold from the hips and let torso, head, and shoulders relax.
Hold opposite elbows if comfortable and breathe into the back body.

setup: From a forward fold, place hands on shins or thighs.
howTo: Lengthen the spine until torso is roughly parallel to the floor or as mobility allows.
Keep neck long, then return to the fold.

setup: Place hands shoulder width and feet hip width; lift hips up and back.
howTo: Push the floor away, keep knees bent if needed, and lengthen the spine.
Pedal heels gently before settling into the hold.

setup: Step one foot forward between hands and lower the back knee.
howTo: Shift hips forward gently while keeping ribs controlled.
Use hands on floor or front thigh and breathe into the front of the rear hip.

setup: From a low lunge, shift hips backward over the rear knee and lengthen the front leg.
howTo: Keep front heel planted, hinge forward with a long spine, and stop before the pelvis tucks hard.

setup: From hands and knees, sit hips toward heels with knees at a comfortable width.
howTo: Reach arms forward or rest them beside the body and let the forehead settle toward the floor.
Breathe into the back and side ribs.

setup: Start on hands and knees.
howTo: Slide one arm under the other with palm up and lower that shoulder/head toward the floor.
Keep hips relatively centered, then unwind slowly.

setup: Lie prone with elbows under or slightly ahead of shoulders and forearms down.
howTo: Press forearms gently into the floor and lengthen the chest forward.
Spread extension through the spine rather than jamming the low back.

setup: Lie on back with knees bent and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh above the knee.
howTo: Stay there or draw the supporting thigh toward the chest.
Keep the crossed foot gently flexed and shoulders relaxed.

setup: Lie on back and bring knees toward chest.
howTo: Let knees fall gently to one side while arms open.
Keep both shoulders as close to the floor as comfortable and breathe into the ribs.

setup: Lie on back and draw knees toward armpits.
howTo: Hold thighs, shins, ankles, or outer feet and keep sacrum heavy.
Gently rock if comfortable.

setup: Lie on back, bring soles of feet together, and allow knees to fall outward.
howTo: Let gravity open the inner thighs without pushing the knees down.
Breathe slowly into abdomen and ribs.

setup: Lie comfortably on back with legs extended and arms slightly away from body.
howTo: Release deliberate stretching and let the whole body relax.
Use slow nasal breathing and a longer exhale.

setup: From seated or supine, position one ankle across the opposite thigh.
howTo: Keep the front knee comfortable and use a version that does not force hip rotation.
Breathe and relax into the glute stretch.

setup: Sit with legs extended or slightly bent and spine tall.
howTo: Hinge from the hips and reach toward shins/feet without yanking.
Keep breathing and soften the knees as needed.

setup: Lie prone with hands near ribs and elbows close.
howTo: Press lightly into the hands while using back muscles to lift the chest a small amount.
Keep pelvis grounded and neck long.

setup: Lie on back with knees bent or legs extended comfortably; place one hand on chest and one on abdomen.
howTo: Inhale quietly through the nose into the lower ribs/abdomen.
Exhale slowly for longer than the inhale and let tension drop.

setup: Lie on back with feet supported on a wall or surface so hips/knees are near 90 degrees.
howTo: Exhale fully enough to feel ribs come down, then inhale quietly into the back/side ribs.
Keep neck and shoulders relaxed.

setup: Lie face down with forehead resting on stacked hands.
howTo: Breathe into the belly and lower ribs so the abdomen gently presses into the floor.
Use slow relaxed breaths.

movementSelectionRules.generalWarmup: Select enough approved warm-up movements to total about 10 minutes; begin easy and finish warm, never fatigued.
movementSelectionRules.mobility: Cover every mandatoryRegion every session. Use roughly 60-70% of the block for full-body coverage and 30-40% for adaptive emphasis.
movementSelectionRules.jointTendonCare: Select low-fatigue approved capacity/control movements. Avoid stacking high local fatigue onto the next Building Day's main tissues.
movementSelectionRules.cardio: Select exactly 10 distinct work movements from the approved cardio work pool per round/session design; insert Easy March in Place after every work slot. Left/right versions may not count as separate work movements.
movementSelectionRules.yoga: Construct a continuous 25-minute flow using only yoga templates whose entry/exit positions connect naturally. Use the reference flow if a valid continuous adaptive flow cannot be assembled.
movementSelectionRules.downregulation: Include daily stomach vacuums, then at least one approved breathing/downregulation movement.

restAndTransitionRules.generalWarmup: No formal rest unless needed for safety; transitions typically 5-15 seconds.
restAndTransitionRules.mobility: Use 5-15 seconds to change positions/sides; no fatigue-driven rest required.
restAndTransitionRules.jointTendonCare: Generally 20-45 seconds between low-fatigue sets or enough time to regain relaxed breathing.
restAndTransitionRules.cardio: 30-second Easy March in Place is the active recovery after every 30-second work movement; no stationary rest between slots. At the end of each 10-minute round, record steps/HR/effort and begin the next round after the logging transition.
restAndTransitionRules.yoga: Every pose must have explicit hold/flow duration and explicit transition duration. Total pose time + transitions must equal exactly 25:00.
restAndTransitionRules.downregulation: No rush between holds/breathing drills; use 10-30 seconds as needed to change position.

fallbackSession.rule: If adaptive generation fails, generate from the approved libraries using the fixed block durations and the reference yoga flow; never create unapproved movements.

runtimeResponsibilities.programCalibration: APP RESPONSIBILITY — on new AI-generated or Phantom/custom program start, determine recommended starting loads from calibration/history. Presets may remain user-selected.
runtimeResponsibilities.workoutDifficultySelector: APP RESPONSIBILITY — user-selected session difficulty modifies runtime recommendations without rewriting exercise selection, set count, order, rest, or legal rep ranges.
runtimeResponsibilities.setBySetAdaptation: APP RESPONSIBILITY — use actual performed load/reps plus 1-5 star set difficulty to recommend the next set inside this program's guardrails.
runtimeResponsibilities.phantomLibraryVisibility: APP RESPONSIBILITY — private Phantom exercises may execute when assigned but must not automatically become browsable by ordinary users.
runtimeResponsibilities.floaterSelectionUI: APP RESPONSIBILITY — prompt once per week for Saturday or Sunday and schedule D4 plus the remaining Rejuvenation day accordingly.

loadLoggingPolicy.plateLoadedMachines: Log external loaded resistance consistently. If carriage/bar resistance is unlabeled, log plates only and keep that convention for that machine profile.
loadLoggingPolicy.cableMachines: Loads are machine-profile-specific and must not transfer blindly between gyms/cable stacks.
loadLoggingPolicy.bodyweightSkills: Log bodyweight and any added belt weight or assistance separately.
